News.title: Mortgage rates hit three-year high as Trump vows more strikes
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Stocks fell heavily and oil prices surged after Donald Trump said other countries would have to “take the lead” in reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Asian markets plunged and European shares were expected to do the same at the start of trading after the US president’s address to the nation.

He told the American people that countries struggling to get fuel should “just take” the Strait of Hormuz shipping route and “use it for yourselves”.

He also urged foreign governments to buy oil from the US until they can reopen the waterway, where a fifth of the world’s oil and gas exports pass.

“The countries of the world that do receive oil through the Hormuz Strait must take care of that passage,” he said.

“They must cherish it. They must grab it and cherish it, they can do it easily.”

Shares had risen sharply and oil had fallen on Tuesday and Wednesday over hopes that the US and Iran were close to ending the Middle East conflict, which has left the shipping route effectively closed.

“Those moves are now revealed as an April Fool’s rally,” said Rabobank analyst Benjamin Picton.

On Wednesday, the main stock markets in Japan and South Korea plunged by more than 2pc and 4pc, respectively, as oil prices leapt by 6pc to more than $107 a barrel.

Mr Picton added: “The market optimism of the last 24 hours was always likely to be misplaced.

“The subtext of Trump’s remarks is that Nato and the Gulf states must get involved in the war to re-open the Strait, or else suffer the consequences of US withdrawal for the world economy.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) The era of cheap oil is over | There is no quick fix to the global energy crisis even if Trump ends his war in Iran

2) Elon Musk launches $1.75trn SpaceX stock market listing | Rocket maker preparing for biggest debut in history despite ongoing instability over Iran war

3) AA urges drivers to slow down to save fuel | Advice means motorists should drive at a top speed of 63mph on motorways this Easter weekend

4) Ryanair chief warns of summer flight cancellations | Michael O’Leary says UK is more exposed to jet fuel shortages than rest of Europe

5) Richard Tice sues Labour donor Dale Vince for libel | Reform deputy leader’s defamation claim is latest development in long-running legal row

What happened overnight

Oil rose more than 6pc and Asian stocks fell after Donald Trump said the US will continue to hit Iran “extremely hard”.

The US president also said in his Wednesday night speech that the US will “finish the job” in Iran soon as “core strategic objectives are nearing completion” and military operations could wrap up soon.

However, stocks fell over concerns that he is preparing to end the war without a deal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz shipping route, which carries a fifth of the world’s oil and gas exports.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 was down 2.6pc to 52,333.79, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 5.2pc to 5,191.62.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.4pc to 24,932.81, the Shanghai Composite index was down 1.1pc to 3,903.98.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 dropped 1.1pc, while Taiwan’s Taiex was trading 1.8pc lower.

Oil prices were sharply higher, with Brent crude, the international standard, up 6.6pc to nearly $108 per barrel.

Gold and silver prices fell. Gold’s price was down 2pc to $4,718.70 per ounce, and silver lost 4.9pc to $72.39 an ounce.

Renewed optimism on Wednesday for a possible end to the Iran war pushed world stocks higher, after Trump said late Tuesday the US military could end its offensive in two to three weeks.

On Wednesday, the S&P 500 added 0.7pc to 6,575.32. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5pc to 46,565.74, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.2pc to 21,840.95.

Sports.title: England’s reliance on Harry Kane has hit new heights ahead of World Cup… but future attack is bright for Three Lions
Sports.content:
CRICKETERS know all about LBW — and yes, as a woman, I’m apparently not supposed to understand the rules.

But England football fans will soon need a new acronym: LBK. Life Beyond Kane.





England’s two friendlies against ­Uruguay and Japan were uninspiring and, in both, Thomas Tuchel’s talisman sat on the Wembley bench nursing a knock.

His absence said everything. Without him, we looked exactly what we were — blunt.

The numbers are stark.

A record 78 goals in 112 internationals is impressive enough, but the more alarming figure is this: Since 2015, Kane has scored or assisted 32 per cent of England’s goals. Nearly one in three.



That’s why Tuchel will be wrapping his 32-year-old in cotton wool, bubble wrap and everything else he can find between now and the summer.

The Dominics — Solanke and Calvert-Lewin — worked hard while Phil Foden was used as a false nine during the friendlies, but the cutting edge wasn’t there.

Only ten English strikers featured in the Prem this season, with Chelsea’s Liam Delap the only one under 26. Danny Welbeck and Calvert-Lewin are the only ones to hit double figures — and both are the wrong side of 30.

Tuchel was right to compare losing Kane to Argentina losing Messi. He isn’t just a striker — he’s the difference.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

There is hope on the horizon — Jay Stansfield, Jonathan Rowe, Ethan Nwaneri, Omari Hutchinson and Arsenal’s teenage winger Max Dowman are all exciting prospects — and Lee Carsley’s back-to-back European Under-21 titles show the pipeline is working.

But that’s tomorrow’s story.

England fans booed at Wembley in midweek, but their misery is nothing compared to Italy’s.

The Azzurri have failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup, going out on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina.



The last time Italy played in a World Cup knockout game was 2006 — when they won it.

Since then, England have had eight Prime Ministers, nine managers, Leicester have won the league — and a pint was £2.45.

The four-time world champs absent again.

Although spare a thought for the fans who did qualify yet can’t afford to go.

World Cup ticket prices haven’t just crept up — they’ve been launched into orbit.



The best seats for the final are pushing £8,000.

Standard tickets are running into the thousands.

This is supposed to be the world’s game, not a corporate jolly for those who can afford it.

There will be a limited number of cheaper tickets, but for most fans they’ll be about as easy to get hold of as a front-row seat at Wimbledon on finals day.

The truth is simple: The very supporters who create the atmosphere — who follow their teams through thick and thin — are being priced out of the game.



It’s shameful.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As for England — just pray for a fit Harry Kane.

Because right now, he is the difference between a tournament and a very expensive short holiday.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes reveals thrilling Cristiano Ronaldo moment at Man Utd which still leaves him with ‘goosebumps’
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES has lifted the lid on Cristiano Ronaldo’s stunning Manchester United return — admitting it still gives him goosebumps.

The United skipper was speaking after matching Ronaldo’s tally of six Premier League Player of the Month awards following a standout March.





But despite hitting that milestone, Fernandes was quick to praise his Portuguese idol.

Bruno was asked on Manchester United’s official website – which Old Trafford occasion still gives Fernandes goosebumps?

He said: “Cristiano is an easy one for me… everyone was looking at him.”

And one moment in particular still sticks with him.



Ronaldo’s dramatic return to Old Trafford in 2021 – where he scored twice against Newcastle in a 4-1 win – left a lasting impression on his Portuguese team-mate.

Fernandes said: “It was an unforgettable day. He comes back, scores two goals and looks like he never left.”

The atmosphere inside the ground was unlike anything he had experienced before.

He added: “The atmosphere in the stadium was crazy that day… everything gives goosebumps still to me.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ronaldo’s return felt like a fairytale for fans, who welcomed their hero back after more than a decade away.

But his second spell did not end the same way.

The forward left United on bad terms, following then gaffer Erik ten Hag‘s consistent decision to bench Ronaldo during their spell together in 2022.

Ronaldo came out in a shocking interview with Piers Morgan discussing his unhappiness at the club and criticising the hierarchy of Manchester United.

The interview was not approved by the club and created a public fallout with the Red Devils.



Ronaldo’s contract was then terminated shortly after the interview, which led him to sign for current club Al Nassr.

Despite that, Fernandes insists the magic of that return will never be forgotten.

Sports.title: I worked 12-hour shifts as Amazon delivery driver… now my ex-mentor is in Chelsea dugout trying to end my FA Cup dream
Sports.content:
ETHON ARCHER used to drop off ­parcels for Amazon — but on Saturday he hopes to deliver a knockout blow on Chelsea.

The Port Vale winger is preparing to take on the ­Premier League millionaires at Stamford Bridge in the FA Cup.





It is a world away from 12-hour shifts driving his van around London before dashing off to play on muddy non-league pitches.

Waiting for him in the Chelsea dugout will be two men who saw Archer’s potential long before he became a pro.

Chelsea assistant Calum McFarlane and Under-21s boss Harry Hudson were his mentors at the Kinetic Academy in Croydon — a programme giving youngsters from marginalised backgrounds a second chance.



The pair also managed him at non-league club Whyteleafe, where McFarlane was Hudson’s No 2.

Archer, who is on loan from Luton, said: “It’s going to be surreal, I can’t wait to meet them again — I haven’t seen them in years.

“They helped me progress my game in a way where I was ready for men’s football.

“It will feel like a full-circle moment. After Sunday league, I secured a place in the Kinetic Academy, a scholarship programme where football runs alongside your education.



“It runs like a professional club’s ­academy. You play against other teams in showcase matches. It was there I met Calum and Harry.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“They helped develop me. Both were so detailed and noticed my strengths and weaknesses.

“Their biggest advice was around mastering the basics.

“Get your decision-making right – know when to take one or two touches, when to take on your man and when to pass.

“I could tell back then as coaches they were too good for that level and were going to progress.



“And, obviously, they’re now working with some of the world’s best talent.

“Calum texted me shortly after the draw was made.

“He said how much he was looking forward to us meeting again.



“It’s going to be great because I owe him and Harry a lot.”

Archer, 23, has been an EFL professional for less than two years – since being snapped up by Cheltenham in July 2024.

The winger spent four years in non-league, also playing for Bedfont Sports, Sutton ­Common Rovers, Horley Town, Raynes Park Vale, Welling, Three Bridges and Torquay.

During that time he was the king of the side-hustle. He worked as a matchday steward for AFC Wimbledon, a host at Boxpark and did night shifts at Iceland.

But it was his stint as an Amazon delivery driver that truly tested his resolve.



He said: “I’d work and have training ­afterwards or a game on a Tuesday night.

“It could get tiring, being on my feet all day, but I chose to do it.

“I ended up quite enjoying it because once you get the hang of it, it’s quite chilled – you’re in your van listening to music and getting out and about.”

After a season with Torquay in National League South, he returned to Amazon to earn extra cash for a holiday.

But he put his delivery driver days behind him when Cheltenham director of football Gary Johnson, his manager at Torquay, signed him for the Robins.



Archer quickly established himself at Whaddon Road before Luton splashed £500,000 last September to sign him.

He was initially loaned back to Cheltenham before returning to Kenilworth Road to train with Jack Wilshere’s men in January.

After joining Port Vale on loan, he helped the Valiants shock Bristol City and Sunderland in the FA Cup to set up this tie.

Archer – whose cousins Mickel Miller and Thierry Small play for Huddersfield and Preston – credits his flair to South London’s “cage football culture.”

During Covid, he spent hours perfecting the skills that now terrify League One defenders – while his non-league schooling taught him to mix technical prowess with the game’s physical side.



He said: “Cage football half-made me the player I am today. It brought out my flair.

“I was there week after week, trying different skills. It was competitive, and there were some good players down there.

“Non-league was also great because it taught me properly about men’s football and it wasn’t all on the floor.



“It’s good to understand other ways of playing.”

Port Vale are dead certs to be relegated from League One – sitting bottom and 14 points adrift of safety.

But the FA Cup has given fans a release with 6,000 heading for West London to face a team 62 places above them in English ­football’s pecking order.

Chelsea fans remember League One team Bradford coming back from 2-0 down to knock them out at Stamford Bridge in 2015.

Now Archer must find a way past the likes of Marc Cucurella and Malo Gusto.



He said: “Everyone is buzzing. We’re proud of what we’ve achieved in the Cup.

“I’ve never been to the Bridge before, so that’s one to cross off the bucket list.

“This sounds crazy but I can’t think these Chelsea players are going to run all over me. If I don’t back myself, who is?

“I will get on the ball and go for it – that’s the best way to play any game.”

Archer will seek a souvenir whatever the result. He admitted: “I’ll definitely want to grab a shirt at the end.



“Regardless of who gets through I have the utmost respect for footballers of their level.

“In terms of shirt swapping, I’d probably try to seek out Cole Palmer – a quality player.”

When Archer scored a 25-yard stunner for Cheltenham against Swindon in December, boss Steve Cotterill described it as good enough to win a World Cup final.

Does he have another in his locker to stun Liam Rosenior’s men?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He laughed: “If I ever hit a ball like that again then fair play.



“But I’d take any kind of goal against Chelsea!”

Sports.title: Chelsea set to rip up controversial youth transfer policy after Enzo Fernandez and Marc Cucurella spark major crisis
Sports.content:
THERE are good reasons why Chelsea have punished Enzo Fernandez for his careless talk, and not Marc Cucurella.

The public criticism of the club by both senior players has only added to the Blues’ problems.





But of the two, Cucurella seems a lot more willing to be part of the solution.

Head coach Liam Rosenior pleaded confidentiality when asked whether vice captain Fernandez had expressed remorse or a renewed desire to stay at the club when informed of his two-match suspension on Friday morning.

Rosenior was more forthcoming about the upshot of his half-hour heart-to-heart with Cucurella on Thursday.

The Blues boss said: “Marc is fully committed, he wants to be here.



“He’s made that very, very clear to me. And he actually believes in where we’re moving forward.”

Rosenior has denied claims of a rift between Fernandez and some members of the dressing room, insisting there is a way back for the Argentina World Cup winner.

Maybe the tough love of being excluded will bring about a change of heart in the midfielder.

But it feels like Fernandez has already checked out of the Chelsea “project.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Not so Cucurella, according to Rosenior. The Blues boss is promising “actions rather than words” in the coming weeks and months which will set the club moving in the right direction again.

Most crucially, it seems Chelsea will this summer tweak their recruitment policy of focusing on young players, which Cucurella blamed for the humbling Champions League exit to Paris Saint-Germain.

Rosenior said: “When you have a process, you have to adjust your process to get to where you want to be.

“We’ve had a lot of conversations, exciting conversations about how we can move things forward this summer.

“So there is not a change, but a progress in our thinking about what’s needed so that we can really really challenge for titles next year, which is what this club deserves.”

The Sun’s Chelsea YouTube channel will be your go-to destination for the latest news, transfer updates, match previews, post-match analysis, exclusive interviews, fan reactions, and breaking stories from Stamford Bridge. Subscribe to The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube now

Captain Reece James recently signed a contract extension on terms which will actually reduce his base salary.

James said talks with the club hierarchy had convinced him the club would win major trophies and he was “fully behind the project.”

Rosenior strongly hinted other players would soon commit themselves to the club with new deals.

The Blues boss said: “You’ll see in the coming weeks, there’ll be things that happen around this football club that will actually speak louder than words, and you’ll see what happens in the next couple of weeks in terms of the commitment of the players to this project.”

Cucurella, despite having signed an improved (but not extended) contract earlier this season, may be among those to pledge renewed allegiance to the cause.



But, as Rosenior says, actions speak louder than words.

And it is action on the pitch which will ultimately decide whether Chelsea players and fans buy into his and the club’s vision.

The Blues boss said: “We’ve lost four games.

“As soon as you don’t win games of football at any club, regardless of the project, people lose faith.

“So we have to restore that, I’m aware.



“There is a noise around the football club that we are in crisis, that I am out of my depth, that I talk nonsense.

“It doesn’t affect what is inside of here and that is what the players need to know as well.

“The reality is we are not far from getting to where we want to be.

“So for me, restoring faith is doing the job I need to do on the training ground, in the meetings, on the training pitch, in the relationships I have with the players.



“Then that shows on the pitch and faith is restored when we win games of football.”

Victory on Saturday over Port Vale, League One’s bottom club, to earn an FA Cup semi-final, should be well within Chelsea’s capabilities without Fernandez.

But overcoming Manchester City on April 12 will undeniably be made tougher by his absence.

Only time will tell whether the show of authority in suspending Fernandez proves to be a turning point for Chelsea and their young head coach.

Rosenior said: “Football is a team game. Enzo and Marc are crucial members of this squad and will continue to be that.



“But there are certain moments where the group is more important than any individual, including myself as the head coach.

“If you want to be successful long term, there has to be a discipline, values, a culture of togetherness, actually about ‘we’ and not ‘me.’

“We’ve made that decision not because I want to take a big stand and show I’m a powerful manager.

“It’s about setting the cultures and values and disciplines that we need to be successful long term.”

Cucurella is more likely than Fernandez to stick around to see if it works.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez and Marc Cucurella have acted like LITTLE TOADS with their cowardly behaviour towards Chelsea
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has been rightly punished for his cowardly behaviour.

Chelsea’s Argentina midfielder and Spain left-back Marc Cucurella both used their inter­national breaks to shaft their club-mates and indulge in some friendly fire.





Maybe what those two said is what all Blues fans were thinking, maybe it was something that needed saying.

One thing that cannot be argued is that it was pathetic.

Did they front up to the English media while wearing their club gear? No.



The pair behaved like little toads and chose to speak where there was zero accountability, no one from the club looking over their shoulder and telling them to wind their necks in.

Fernandez and Cucurella decided to use the safety blanket of their national squads to sound off about the decision to sack Enzo Maresca and the approach their club they play for is taking.

And these are two of Chelsea’s supposed leaders. But this is not leadership, it is arse-covering and self-serving hot air.

Both of them will have thought that — after losing four on the bounce before the break — they could go back and, if everything continued to go wrong, they could tell everyone, ‘I told you so’.



They can say that they pointed out that they wouldn’t have sacked Maresca, that everything was better then. But there are problems with that stance, too.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Firstly, the players would not, and should not, have been consulted over the decision to give Maresca his marching orders on New Year’s Day.

And, more importantly, these are the same players who got Chelsea into that mess in the first place.

Was everything better when Maresca was about?



If so, why did you lose at home to Brighton, Sunderland and Aston Villa?

They are trying to revise what happened under the Italian after buying into their own hype off the back of winning two tin-pot trophies last season.

We have had two years of noise around Chelsea being the coming force, a young and exciting squad destined for the top. Now, when the pressure has cranked up since Christmas, this supposedly brilliant squad has started to crack.

Their supposed leaders are showing their selfish side.

Both Fernandez and Cucurella are undeniably big players for the club and talented to boot.



One thing which could well have been the catalyst for their outbursts is a new deal for Reece James. The Chelsea skipper is comfortably the best player at the club when he is available.

But that issue of availability has arisen once again, with his new six-year deal followed almost immediately by another hamstring injury for the 26-year-old.

James has been fantastic for Chelsea but he has played nowhere near as much as Fernandez or Cucurella over the past two years.

Because of that, both of them will be wondering where their shiny new deals are. That is what players care about.

They know James is talented but if he isn’t playing that won’t matter a jot to them.



Cucurella, 27, was given better terms last year but not longer on his contract. And Fernandez is waiting on talks over his own future, having cast it into doubt.

All of this is symptomatic of the club Chelsea have become under this ownership. There are so many owners, directors and big figures upstairs that there is next to no authority or accountability.

I cannot see anyone in that squad who would have grabbed the pair by the scruff of the neck when they returned this week and told them to get their act together.

Back when I was a captain, had a team-mate behaved like this you would be telling the manager not to call fouls in training and let the pair know what you really thought of them at the first opportunity.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In axing Fernandez, 25, from his squad for tomorrow’s FA Cup quarter-final with Port Vale and Manchester City next week in the Prem, boss Liam Rosenior may finally be grasping the accountability issue.



But at a club which just cannot get out of its own way, where they are making the noise rather than shutting it out, the issues run very deep indeed.

Sports.title: Moises Caicedo becomes THIRD Chelsea superstar to drop transfer exit bombshell as he talks up Real Madrid move
Sports.content:
MOISES CAICEDO is the latest Chelsea player to raise doubts over his future after Enzo Fernandez was BANNED for his comments.

The Blues’ midfielder refused to rule out a potential exit, leaving the door open to a move away.





In an interview with Spanish outlet AS, Caicedo was asked about Real Madrid and a possible transfer.

He replied: “You never know in football, don’t you think?

“I have a contract with Chelsea now.

“The truth is, I haven’t honestly thought about another club, about leaving London, but well, in the end, you never know in football.

“All I want is to enjoy myself. I have a contract and I want to keep playing as long as God allows.

“After that, we’ll see what happens. I have a contract, but we’ll see what the future holds. Let’s see what surprises await us.”

Caicedo, 24, is the third Chelsea player to be asked about his long-term commitment to the club in recent weeks after partner Fernandez caused outrage.

The Argentine said multiple times over the international break that he would love to live in Madrid, just days after he admitted he wasn’t sure what the summer held for him.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandez has been linked with PSG and Los Blancos heavily in the fortnight since with Marc Cucurella openly asked about a return to Barcelona as well.

Defender Cucurella, 27, is another member of Chelsea’s leadership team alongside Fernandez and Caicedo.

He, like Fernandez, called out the club’s youth transfer policy and the events which led to Enzo Maresca leaving.

Only Fernandez was suspended internally for his interviews, especially due to the repeated nature, but it does not help the already unsettled atmosphere at Chelsea.



Caicedo, whilst playing down a big-money deal elsewhere, has far from shut down leaving at what is a sensitive time for fans.

Many are already frustrated at the ownership and sporting directors, actually choosing to side with disillusioned players instead.

Although Caicedo is tied down on terms until 2031 with the option to extend that for another 12 months, Chelsea are aware that their best players will expect Champions League football.

Under Liam Rosenior there is now a distinct chance that will not get delivered next season.



It would be the third time in four years under Clearlake Capital-Todd Boehly that Chelsea have missed out on UCL football, even with the added security of a fifth-place qualifying from the Prem.

Fernandez, who has been the most vocal and is vice-captain – currently wearing the armband in Reece James‘ absence – could even go later this year.

His agent, former PSG midfielder Javier Pastore, told The Athletic: “Our plan after the World Cup is to meet with Chelsea again and, if there is no agreement, to explore other options.”

Fernandez will miss Chelsea’s games against Port Vale and Manchester City due to his punishment, something that Pastore also hit out at.

He said: “Enzo didn’t understand the situation.



“When the coach told him, he accepted it because he’s a highly professional guy who’s always fully committed wherever he is and respects decisions, but we don’t understand the punishment because he doesn’t mention any club or say he wants to leave Chelsea, far from it.”

Sports.title: Man City top league of football clubs with most drug seizures in 2025 – is your team among the worst offenders?
Sports.content:
POLICE sniffed out more drugs at Man City’s Etihad Stadium than any other ground last year.

The 60 stops were well clear of second place Manchester United’s 38.

Championship side Charlton Athletic were third with 32.





Chelsea (24) and Brighton (17) completed the top five, the study of data from England and Wales police forces found.

Overall there were 386 drug seizures at matches in 2025. The substances included cocaine, cannabis, ketamine and ecstasy.

But the true number will be much higher because only 19 of the 43 forces responded.

Sniffer dogs are routinely deployed at grounds amid fears drugs are fuelling violence.

Other clubs in the top ten were QPR (16 seizures), Brentford (14), Leeds (11), and Newcastle and Oxford (six each).

One suspect was nabbed trying to sneak into Brighton’s Amex stadium with magic mushrooms.

The UK Football Policing Unit said: “The increase in arrests and football banning orders demonstrates that the police are taking positive action to tackle the problems. We collectively need to make football a safe environment for the overwhelming majority of fans.”

But Michael Brunskill, of the Football Supporters’ Association, said: “Arrest figures are considerably lower than comparable music or street festivals.



“I certainly feel safer there with my kids than I would in city centres on a Saturday night.”

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney ready to swap £400k Match of the Day role for dugout return next season despite Birmingham & Plymouth flops
Sports.content:
EX-ENGLAND star and TV pundit Wayne Rooney is open to getting back into football management for the start of next season.

The star’s ambitions were revealed as wife Coleen celebrated her 40th birthday with a party in a giant marquee at their mansion yesterday.





Former Man United and Everton ace Roo has worked in the media since he left his head coach job at Plymouth Argyle in December 2024 after a poor run of results.

He bagged a £400,000-a-year role as a Match of the Day pundit after impressing BBC bosses.

But The Sun understands he now fancies his chances again as a boss in either the Championship or League One.

A source said: “Wayne is enjoying his telly work, but he does want to get back into management. He will be open to it if the right opportunity comes up.



“Ideally, he would get something at the start of the summer so he is in position for the start of the season in August.”

Wayne, also 40, declared himself wife Coleen’s No1 fan yesterday as they hosted the VIP Cheshire bash for her birthday.

And he shared pictures online from their 25-year relationship.

Among them were photos of the couple with their four sons Kai, 16, Klay, 12, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.



He wrote: “Happy 40th Birthday to the best wife and mum we could wish for. We can’t wait to celebrate with you and love you all the world”.

Sir David and Victoria Beckham were rumoured to be attending, alongside other former teammates including Ryan Giggs, Paul ­Scholes, Darren Fletcher, Peter Crouch and wife Abbey Clancy and United boss Michael Carrick. Some guests arrived by helicopter.

A source said: “No expense was spared for Coleen’s big birthday. She wanted to go all out.”

Wayne signed his two-year Match of the Day contract at the beginning of the 2025/26 season after host Gary Lineker left.

Rooney scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances and 253 goals for United. But his managerial career was less glorious.



He joined Derby County as a player in January 2020, before being appointed manager a year later, but they were relegated to League One having been in administration and suffering a 21-point deduction.

He resigned in June 2022 and joined DC United in the US the next month, but left at the end of the season.

He joined Birmingham City in October 2023, then lost his job the following January.

Plymouth came calling in May 2024, but he left by mutual ­consent seven months later.

Sports.title: Arne Slot launches passionate rant on Mo Salah's Liverpool exit - 'Careful with assumptions!'
Sports.content:
Arne Slot launches passionate rant on Mo Salah's Liverpool exit - 'Careful with assumptions!'

Mohamed Salah has decided to leave Liverpool at the end of the season, months after a very public falling out with manager Arne Slot over his lack of game time and poor form

View 3 Images Arne Slot spoke at length about the perception of Mo Salah's decision to leave Liverpool (Image: This Is Anfield)

Arne Slot says he has no regrets over the way he handled the Mohamed Salah fallout earlier this season - and insisted it is not behind his exit from Liverpool this summer.

‌



Salah announced recently that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season. The 33-year-old will bow out at the end of a difficult campaign which saw him publicly call out Slot for leaving him on the bench. Back in December, Salah said his manager had "thrown me under the bus" by blaming him for the team's poor form.

‌



After being benched for three straight games, Salah claimed "there is no relationship" between himself and Slot and that "someone doesn’t want me in the club". The two eventually repaired their relationship, with Salah returning to the side and Slot remains convinced he handled the situation as best he could.

‌



"I look back at this season thinking that I made a few decisions that could have been better but I’m not talking about this specific thing with Mo," Slot said in Friday's press conference ahead of Liverpool's FA Cup quarter final against Manchester City.

"I don't regret many things I did during a little longer than one-and-a-half years together. Again, the assumption that if he's not playing that he wants to leave - that's the assumption being made - then he would have left one-and-a-half years ago.

‌



"I can remember West Ham away when he wasn't playing (under Jurgen Klopp in 2024). I wasn't there. He didn’t decide to leave. The assumption is that if you don’t play in these games and all of a sudden wants to leave, it is an assumption and maybe it is true or maybe it isn’t. But history has shown is that he did not do that previously and had a great season after that.

"When things like this are announced to the outside world, I don't think it's a surprise for you to hear that there are a lot of discussions, talks going on between him, his agent, the club, me and him, before this comes out in the public.

"But, as I always said, and I'm not going to change on what has been said between the two of us, or between him and the club, that is something I'm not going to share.

‌



View 3 Images Mohamed Salah was fed up at being on the bench earlier in the season (Image: Getty)

"If he wants to share his reasons why he did it then it's up to him, but that's not up to me to speak for him. I hear a lot being said about Liverpool and one of the funny things about Liverpool is that almost everything that is out there is not true.

"What I mean is I see sometimes that we are trying to sign players. I'm like, ‘what is everybody talking about? We're not even considering the player or even talking about him at all?’ I think that's a big, big compliment to the people who work here.

‌



"Even when I signed, there were a lot of other names mentioned when I already knew I already signed. So that says something about Liverpool."

Slot also hinted that there was more to the situation that hadn't been made public. He added: "So what appears to be true, especially in terms of Liverpool, is maybe not always true. I think Mo has earned the right completely to decide whenever he thinks he should leave. And he's done so many things for this club. He has to make up his own mind and that's what he did.

View 3 Images Arne Slot spoke at length about Mo Salah (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

‌



"After that incident you are referring to [at Leeds], which are incidents that happen everywhere around the world almost every day when it comes to football, you know what has happened afterwards? He went to the AFCON and when he was back at the AFCON, he played every single game.

"So that's the answer to your question. The only one who can talk about it is Mo himself. So you are now making the assumption that he wants to leave because he was out for six days. But that doesn't have to be true.

"I would be surprised if there's not moment when Mo's going to share his thoughts about why he made the decision he made. It's not up to me to do that. It's up to him. And I would not go into all these assumptions, and I would be, how do you say this in English? I would be careful with assumptions, yes."

Sports.title: Arne Slot makes 'probably impossible' admission over replacing Mo Salah at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Arne Slot makes 'probably impossible' admission over replacing Mo Salah at Liverpool

Liverpool will be left with a huge void in their squad when Mohamed Salah leaves the club at the end of the season and Arne Slot has called on other players to step up

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah is leaving Liverpool at the end of the season (Image: Getty)

Arne Slot has admitted that finding a single player to replace Mohamed Salah is "probably impossible" and that Liverpool will instead turn to last summer's recruits to step up when he leaves. Salah will walk away from Liverpool after nine years this summer, leaving a huge hole that needs filling.

‌



The 33-year-old forward recently announced he will leave at the end of the season, having won two Premier League titles and the Champions League, among many other honours. He has scored 255 goals for the club - the third most of any player - and will go down in the club's history as one of their best ever players.

‌



Even in a difficult campaign, Salah has contributed 10 goals and nine assists in 34 appearances across all competitions this season. And Liverpool fans will miss his trademark of cutting inside from the right wing to curl into the net with his left foot.

‌



Liverpool spent £320million on attacking reinforcements last summer, in the form of Florian Wirtz, Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak, and Slot says the bulk of the responsibility for replacing Salah's output will fall on their shoulders.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Dominik Szoboszlai gives update on Liverpool future after Real Madrid transfer links READ MORE :

Alisson issues injury denial after Liverpool boss Arne Slot gives worrying return timeline READ MORE :

"Of course we do," Slot said on Friday when asked if Liverpool had a plan for replacing Salah. "We are not starting to work on it now because we are constantly working on where we can improve. There is not a lot talked about this but it is 88 minutes that Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz were together on the pitch together.

‌



"So let’s first find out and work out how that works together and that can give us so much more. It is never one player who can replace Mo. Otherwise there would be 15 or 20 Mo’s and he is one of a kind, which is why he is so special.

"You cannot find a Mo replacement. Maybe you can but he would not be available. Yes I am [involved in summer planning]. I know why you ask this question."

View 3 Images Arne Slot will demand more from Alexander Isak next season (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



While getting the best out of last summer's recruits is a priority, Slot also feels that the role of the Premier League winger has also changed so much that players in Salah's mould will become rarer and rarer.

He added: "How the league has changed is maybe not so much to do with the winger position that we need to recruit. But we are aware that football has changed in England. We will always try to have our own style, but we cannot shut our eyes for the new reality and that is that it's not only low blocks, it's also set-piece after set-piece after set-piece.

"One of the reasons why we haven't been successful in the first half of the season was mainly set-pieces. Yes, I'm fully involved in next season and we have these discussions as well. How can we unlock a low block? Now, the England manager (Thomas Tuchel) has an opinion about that.

‌



View 3 Images Mohamed Salah is leaving Liverpool at the end of the season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

"Wingers are very important to unlock a load block, as we noticed last season with Mo and Luis Diaz. But there are more things that you have to be aware of like set-piece, defending all these long throw-ins and all these pieces that teams do.

"Maybe having someone that has a long throw-in because when we had this with Joe Gomez we immediately scored against Nottingham Forest. So you try to make the team as best as possible, and that's why replacing Mo on a one-on-one is probably impossible.

"So we have to find a way of making it work that the team is stronger but it would already make our team much stronger if we've got Alex, Hugo and Florian together available for a bit more than 88 minutes this year."

Sports.title: Mo Salah's net worth, wife's complaint about him and house that 'looks like hospital'
Sports.content:
Mo Salah's net worth, wife's complaint about him and house that 'looks like hospital'

Liverpool star Mohamed Salah is one of the world's most famous footballers, and his personal life reflects that status

View 4 Images Mohamed Salah is a Premier League icon (Image: DARREN STAPLES/AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool icon Mohamed Salah has become one of the most famous faces in world football during his glittering career with the Reds. After arriving from Roma in 2017, few expected the impact the winger would have on the club and the English game.

‌



Under Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot, Salah has won two Premier League titles, the Champions League, the FA Cup, two Carabao Cups, the UEFA Super Cup, the FIFA Club World Cup, and the Community Shield. He has also won a host of personal accolades.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



However, after almost nine years, his time at the club is set to come to an end in the summer, following his decision to leave earlier this month. With his global status comes massive wealth and luxury. Here, Mirror Football takes a closer look at the man dubbed 'The Egyptian King', from his net worth to his personal life.

Salah's net worth

According to Celebrity Net Worth, Salah's net worth stands at £68million. His income stems from his lucrative Liverpool contracts, which have seen him earn at least £18m per year since 2022 and roughly £10m per year since 2018.

While Salah is now in the last few months of his life on Merseyside, he only signed on to extend his stay with Liverpool for another two years in May 2025. That deal was reportedly worth a stunning £350,000 per week.

‌



Steven Gerrard reveals frank Mohamed Salah text messages and backs his Liverpool exit READ MORE :

He also has several endorsement deals with global brands, including Adidas, Pepsi, Vodafone, and Audi. It's also understood that when image rights and commercial activities are taken into account, Salah can earn a further £1m per week.

Stunning house

Salah is believed to reside in Cheshire's exclusive 'golden triangle' area. The forward has converted his home to accommodate his rigorous fitness routine.

The house is noted for having extensive workout facilities, including multiple gym rooms, a hyperbaric chamber, and cryotherapy. Salah often shares photos from inside the property, which features a huge garden and plenty of spacious living areas.

‌



4 View 4 Images Salah has released several photos with his wife and children from their luxury home (Image: Instagram) 4 View 4 Images Mohamed Salah often provides updates from his home gym (Image: Instagram)

Every Christmas, he posts pictures of his family in front of a Christmas tree and also marks Eid with his household. Other footballers known to live in the luxurious 'golden triangle' are Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk and Man City star Erling Haaland.

‌



Wife's complaint

While Salah and his partner Magi are happily married, the Liverpool star's long-term partner is said to have one complaint: the surgical-looking house they both share.

Magi has remained a devoted companion to the Egyptian icon and is the mother to their two daughters, Makka and Kayan. Salah, 32, met Magi when the pair were school kids living in the Egyptian village of Basion Gharbia.

View 4 Images Mohamed Salah and his wife Magi Salah with their children (Image: Getty)

‌



However, in an interview with France Football, Salah opened up on the areas of his home he has dedicated to his personal fitness, to his wife's dismay.

"Two rooms in our house are dedicated to different fitness machines, bodybuilding," he explained. "At home I can also do cryotherapy, there is a hyperbaric chamber. I am constantly looking to improve my physical condition. It's true that I like to say that my house looks like a hospital, [but] my wife doesn't like that! [She] says that I spend more time with my machines than with her!"

It underscores the extent of their union that Magi has embraced the clinical atmosphere of their mansion to maximise her husband's playing career.

Sports.title: Moises Caicedo addresses Chelsea future after Enzo Fernandez punishment - 'The truth is'
Sports.content:
Moises Caicedo addresses Chelsea future after Enzo Fernandez punishment - 'The truth is'

Chelsea have been rocked by Enzo Fernandez's comments in the international break and now fellow star midfielder Moises Caicedo has openly spoken about Real Madrid

View 2 Images Moises Caicedo has spoken about his future plans (Image: Chelsea FC/Getty Images)

Chelsea star Moises Caicedo failed to rule out a potential transfer to Real Madrid when asked about where his career may take him. The Blues have been rocked by captain Enzo Fernandez flirting with Real - and now Caicedo has added to the uncertainty around the squad.

‌



Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior has decided to drop Fernandez for the next two matches, saying "a line was crossed" in his recent comments. The Argentina international admitted he liked Madrid and would like to live in Spain. Fernandez's agent has branded his punishment "completely unfair".

‌



His words come amid a difficult period for Chelsea, with four straight defeats seeing them knocked out of the Champions League by Paris Saint-Germain and drop to sixth in the Premier League. Rosenior has tried to steady the ship ahead of Saturday's FA Cup quarter final against Port Vale, but there is clearly discontent in the ranks, with Marc Cucurella also speaking out during the international break.

‌



Caicedo is another key player for Rosenior and his words, while away on international duty with Ecuador in Madrid, won't help matters. "You never know in football, don't you think?" Caicedo told AS when asked if he could imagine himself wearing the white of Real Madrid.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I have a contract with Chelsea now. The truth is, I haven't honestly thought about another club, about leaving London, but well, in the end, you never know in football.

‌



"All I want is to enjoy myself. I have a contract and I want to keep playing as long as God allows. After that, we'll see what happens. I have a contract, but we'll see what the future holds. Let's see what surprises await us."

Caicedo has made 139 appearances for Chelsea since joining in a £115million move from Brighton in August 2023. He is under contract until June 2031 and did make it clear that he is happy in west London.

View 2 Images Chelsea have been rocked by Enzo Fernandez's comments (Image: PA)

‌



"Chelsea is a great club," he added. "They've helped me a lot since I arrived. I want to repay them, to show it in every game, for as long as I'm there. And well, time will tell."

Chelsea defender Cucurella spoke openly about how the squad had struggled since Enzo Maresca was replaced by Rosenior in January. And Caicedo made a similar point when asked about their current situation.

"Yes, it's a little difficult because we were with a coach we were used to playing with, with his style," he said. "But now we have Rosenior with us. It's been a bit of a struggle to adapt, it's true, but I know it's just a matter of time to get used to something new.

Article continues below

"Sometimes you adapt faster, sometimes it takes a little longer. Anyway. I think the whole team is going through a tough time right now, yes. We have to keep going, we have to try to get through this, the season, because we have a lot of great things ahead of us."

Sports.title: Roy Hodgson wins first game as Bristol City manager and his reaction speaks volumes
Sports.content:
Roy Hodgson wins first game as Bristol City manager and his reaction speaks volumes

Aged 78, Roy Hodgson has taken charge of Championship side Bristol City until the end of this season, and the former England boss won his first game back in the dugout

View 2 Images Roy Hodgson got off to a winning start (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Humble Roy Hodgson didn't want showering with praise after leading Bristol City to victory in his first game at the helm. Hodgson, 78, was appointed by the Robins last week, more than four decades after his first spell at the club.

‌



In charge until the end of this season, the former England manager's first task was a trip to The Valley to face Charlton Athletic. City got off to a dream start after only 11 minutes, with Scott Twine giving them an early lead.

‌



Lyndon Dykes equalised for Charlton on the half-hour mark, but a goal from Noah Eile, thanks to a dreadful error by goalkeeper Will Mannion, restored the visitors' lead. Hodgson's resolute side were able to hold onto all three points and have moved up to 13th in the Championship table, ending a run of six games without a win under former boss Gerhard Struber.

‌



Post-match, Hodgson heaped praise on his players. "I was pleased for the team. I was pleased with the way that they went about trying to win the game," he said via the Bristol Post.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Joachim Low sets record straight on Ghana job claims ahead of England World Cup clash READ MORE :

Harry Kane ruled out as Bayern Munich sweat on injury ahead of Real Madrid clash READ MORE :

"I thought in the first half, and in the second half, before the onslaught started, we were looking really good value for a victory. Also, I must take my hat off to that backline, the goalkeeper and the midfield players for surviving the onslaught.

‌



"I'm afraid that the cult of the manager, the cult of the coach is something that I tend to play down. It's football players that win it. If you're going to win, you need quality in your team."

Hodgson has managed 22 different clubs and countries across his nomadic coaching career which has now spanned 50 years. It was thought that he wouldn't manage again after leaving Crystal Palace in February 2024, having fallen ill in the days leading up to his departure.

Does Roy Hodgson's career deserve more acclaim? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Roy Hodgson was delighted with his players (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Even though Hodgson has ruled out a long-term stay at Ashton Gate, he looked fit for the fight on the touchline. "I've learned a lot," he added. "Don't forget, this is the first time I've seen these seriously play live, so I've learned a lot.

"I think they should be proud of the fact that they came away with the three points, and I personally thought, certainly for large periods of the game, we were more deserving of it."

Article continues below

City's next game is on Monday at home to Sheffield United. They'll then return to London to take on Queens Park Rangers next Saturday.

Sports.title: Pep Lijnders broke Jurgen Klopp promise after leaving Liverpool and joining Manchester City
Sports.content:
Pep Lijnders broke Jurgen Klopp promise after leaving Liverpool and joining Manchester City

Pep Lijnders was one of Jurgen Klopp's closest colleagues but he broke the promise he made the former Reds boss

View 3 Images Pep Lijnders went from working with Jurgen Klopp to Pep Guardiola (Image: Getty Images)

Pep Lijnders went back on the promise he made Jurgen Klopp by becoming a key confidant of Pep Guardiola. The ex-Liverpool coach left Anfield alongside the German at the end of the 2023/24 season.

‌



Once again making the venture into head coaching, the Dutchman signed a three-year deal at RB Salzburg in May 2024 but lasted just seven months after he was sacked shortly before the turn of the year.

‌



Opting to stay out of football until next summer, Lijnders' next role stunned the Liverpool fanbase as he joined Manchester City to become one of Guardiola's assistant managers, alongside former City and Liverpool defender Kolo Toure.

‌



In deciding to join forces with the legendary Spaniard who labelled Klopp as his greatest-ever rival, Lijnders broke the promise he made to Klopp. After leaving Liverpool for the second time, the 43-year-old insisted he would never be an assistant to anyone else and pledged his focus towards his managerial career.

He said at the time: "10 years of the club and my boys don’t know anything else, they are Scousers. I owe this club everything. They don’t owe me anything, to be honest.

Jurgen Klopp opens up on special Anfield return in unique Kenny Dalglish moment READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp comparison made as Arne Slot handed Liverpool sack verdict READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"It’s 10 years full of dedication. I always said I will finish with Jurgen (Klopp); the moment I will not assist anyone else, that’s the moment I will go and I will manage. That was always the case. So when we spoke, it was clear for me: OK, then I go and manage, and we end this project together [that] we started.

"It’s not easy. My boys, my wife; my boys are two proper Scousers and their whole life they will be. Maybe posh ones! But still! I cannot say thank you enough to everybody involved."

View 3 Images Pep Lijnders joined forces with Pep Guardiola at Manchester City last summer (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



Prior to City's 2-1 win over Liverpool in February, Guardiola opened up about his decision to hire Lijnders, admitting he felt an instant connection with the Dutchman. The City boss said: "I had a lot of info from other people about him who had been trained or managed by him at Liverpool.

"I needed to refresh myself first with new people who have incredible knowledge about the game and the Premier League and I love a lot many things that he did with Jurgen at Liverpool.

"We talked one day, I think we felt connected immediately. I am incredibly lucky that since the first day I started as a manager [with] all my backroom staff and close people and Pep is one of them."

‌



View 3 Images Lijnders worked with Klopp for almost the entirety of the German's Anfield reign (Image: Getty Images)

Lijnders' contribution to the Citizens this season has already brought silverware with City defeating Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final last month. A domestic cup double is still on the cards with City hosting Liverpool on Saturday in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup.

It'll be Lijnders on the touchline managing City as he aims to knock his ex-club out of the competition with Guardiola serving a two-match ban.

Sports.title: 11 players could miss Man City vs Liverpool after Arne Slot and Pep Guardiola injury updates
Sports.content:
11 players could miss Man City vs Liverpool after Arne Slot and Pep Guardiola injury updates

Liverpool take on Man City in the FA Cup quarter-final at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon

View 2 Images Man City and Liverpool could both be missing players for Saturday's FA Cup clash

Both Arne Slot and Pep Guardiola have given injury updates ahead of tomorrow's FA Cup quarter-final clash between Manchester City and Liverpool at the Etihad Stadium. City host the Reds fresh off the international break and their Carabao Cup triumph over Arsenal at Wembley Stadium.

‌



In contrast, Liverpool have struggled to repeat their title-winning form from last season and were beaten 3-1 by Brighton ahead of the international break, but are missing several key players through injury. Slot has delivered some major Liverpool injury updates ahead of the game.

‌



There were concerns regarding four players both before and during the international break, with hopes of a comeback for Alexander Isak growing over the coming weeks following Slot's latest assessment.

‌



Alisson issues injury denial after Liverpool boss Arne Slot gives worrying return timeline READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta's blunt verdict after Arsenal star Ben White suffers England boos READ MORE :

Speaking on Friday, the Liverpool boss said: "It will definitely be too fast to expect him in the starting line-up. He trained with us yesterday for the first time, and today, for the second time after exactly 101 days. So, it will take a bit of time... we will make sure we do the right thing in terms of building him up."

Mohamed Salah is among those who could feature from the start at the Etihad Stadium, with Slot delivering an encouraging update after the Egyptian missed the defeat to Brighton and his country's international fixtures.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The Liverpool head coach confirmed: "He is [fit]. He trained with us yesterday, he will train with us today and is available for the game tomorrow."

There was further positive news regarding Federico Chiesa and Jeremie Frimpong following their respective stints with Italy and the Netherlands. Chiesa returned to Liverpool early, while Frimpong was withdrawn just 13 minutes after coming on against Ecuador due to a potential injury concern, but Slot confirmed both players were back in training on Thursday

The 47-year-old was unable to offer any encouraging news regarding Alisson, with the shot-stopper set to sit out Liverpool's next four matches at the very minimum due to a hamstring problem.

‌



View 2 Images Alisson spoke out on his injury (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Slot said: "He will not be part of the Paris Saint-Germain games as well. He will be out for a bit longer. Towards the end of the season, we expect him to be fit again."

Alisson had only recently returned from a brief spell on the sidelines but has now rejoined several other long-term Liverpool injury casualties.

‌



Taking to social media platform X on Friday afternoon, the goalkeeper posted his own update, writing: "I didn't suffer a new injury. I'm in the treatment phase, and the plan is to be in full playing condition by the end of April!"

Wataru Endo, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have all gone under the knife this season, with none of the three expected to feature again this campaign.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Pep Guardiola has considerably fewer fitness worries ahead of the FA Cup showdown between Liverpool and City. Josko Gvardiol remains their sole confirmed long-term absentee, while fellow defenders John Stones and Ruben Dias are also nursing concerns.

The latter missed the Carabao Cup final against Arsenal through a hamstring complaint, but having enjoyed several weeks of rest, he could find himself in Saturday's squad.

Greater uncertainty surrounds John Stones following his withdrawal from the England squad earlier this week, with Thomas Tuchel delivering an injury assessment upon his return to Man City.

Article continues below

He said: "John was gutted he had this minor incident, not a big injury. Given the history, we had to be careful; it made no sense to push him through and try stuff that could make it worse."

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai gives update on Liverpool future after Real Madrid transfer links
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai gives update on Liverpool future after Real Madrid transfer links

Dominik Szoboszlai has been the standout player for Arne Slot's side in a difficult season - and the Liverpool star's form has seen him linked with a move to Real Madrid

View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has spoken about his happiness at Liverpool (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Dominik Szoboszlai has confirmed that he is happy at Liverpool and not considering a summer exit following links with Real Madrid. Szoboszlai has been in superb form for Liverpool this season and talk of a departure had worried fans.

‌



The Hungary international has been the standout player for Arne Slot's side during a difficult campaign. He has contributed 12 goals and eight assists in 43 appearances across all competitions, despite often filling in at right-back due to injuries.

‌



He only arrived on Merseyside in 2023, yet Hungary manager Marco Rossi claimed recently that Szoboszlai has always 'dreamed' of playing for Real Madrid. Rossi's comments came after Real's Vinicius Junior revealed that he's friends with Szoboszlai and regularly messages him.

‌



That speculation led to suggestions of a move to Real this summer, with Liverpool's Premier League title defence having fallen apart. But Szoboszlai himself says that is not on the cards.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

What FSG really think about sacking Arne Slot as Liverpool owners hatch summer plan READ MORE :

Alisson issues injury denial after Liverpool boss Arne Slot gives worrying return timeline READ MORE :

"I love being here," he told the Liverpool Echo at the Easter lunch of Merseyside charity Football For Change. "My family is happy, I love the club, I love the fans, I love to play for this club and that is it."

‌



Szoboszlai is under contract with Liverpool until June 2028 and has shone both as a midfielder and at right-back this season. His impact, including some long-range free-kicks, have won acclaim amongst the Anfield faithful and he is delighted with how it's going.

"I knew [how big Liverpool was], actually, but once you are inside you realise properly what it does mean to be a Liverpool player," he said. "It was unbelievable because I still remember I had to choose my shirt number and I knew that Naby [Keita] was no longer here, so No.8 was free.

"So that was an easy choice. Then, when I stepped into the training ground, seeing how everything is there and what kind of players are playing here, it was just a dream come true for me."

‌



View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has earned comparisons with Steven Gerrard (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

The 25-year-old's iconic shirt number and driving performances in the middle of the park has seen some compare him with Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard. "It is a big compliment," Szoboszlai said.

"But I've many times that I just try to do my own story and sometimes we struggle as a team but we always try to put everything on the pitch and then this season I do stuff off the pitch, trying to help the new guys, coming from different leagues.

‌



"I know how it feels to be new and I know how hard it is to come to the Premier League and especially Liverpool where you are always expected to win trophies.

"I hope [I am becoming a leader] but you have to ask someone else how they see it but I try to do my best on and off the pitch, try to keep everyone [together], try to be a leader [with] what I am doing on the pitch and that is the most important thing for me. Hopefully we can change this season in a good way."

Sports.title: Championship talking points: Millwall blow autos race open; Coventry move 11 points clear
Sports.content:
Millwall in dreamland after Boro blow big chances again

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship game between Middlesbrough and Millwall.

Middlesbrough 1-2 Millwall

Thirty-two shots. Sixty-nine touches in the opposition box. An xG of 3.12. Yet Middlesbrough were beaten at home again.

It was 34 shots, 86 touches in the box and 2.3xG when Boro lost to Millwall's south London neighbours Charlton at the Riverside last month. Their repeated failure to capitalise in the final third has cost them again.

This time it really hurts because Millwall have leapfrogged them into second and an automatic promotion place. "Over time it will turn," said Boro boss Kim Hellberg, who could scarcely believe his side had lost after complete dominance in the first half. But time is running out.

And Millwall may have timed their run perfectly. For the first time this season they go into the top two.

It's dreamland for their supporters. They went into back-to-back away days with Ipswich and Boro knowing it could define the narrative of their run-in.

Four points and two second-half fightbacks later, a first-ever promotion to the Premier League is now a serious possibility.

"We'll see over the next six games how big a win it is but at the moment it feels like a huge win," Lions boss Alex Neil said.

His side will need to take this momentum into a tricky Easter Monday home game with in-form Norwich. But a win there really would set them up, with a favourable schedule of fixtures to finish the campaign…

Peter Smith

Coventry show resolve again to get the job done and move further clear

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Coventry City and Derby County.

Coventry 3-2 Derby

Another step closer for Coventry City. Another hurdle overcome.

The jubilant scenes at the CBS Arena on Friday night showed how far they have come from that dip earlier in 2026, when they briefly fell below Middlesbrough in the Championship table.

Twice they were pegged back by Derby, and on both occasions they responded. The third, and winner, was the most impressive, coming just moments after Ben Brereton Diaz had converted his second of the night from a penalty that was controversial in its award.

It is 11 points clear at the top of the Championship now. Ipswich having two games in hand complicates things a little, but the main message is that Coventry are just eight points away from guaranteeing their place in the Premier League.

That period of 25 years without top-flight football will soon be over.

Simeon Gholam

Wrexham fail to take full advantage of Saints not playing

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between West Bromwich Albion and Wrexham.

West Brom 2-2 Wrexham

Ultimately it was a good point for Wrexham, as they battled back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with West Brom.

It took them above Southampton into sixth, with the Saints in FA Cup action this weekend and not back in Championship battle until they visit Wrexham on Tuesday night.

But it may also have felt like an opportunity missed for the Red Dragons, and leaves things very finely poised heading into that blockbuster clash.

"There was a fantastic response after the break because we were a bit passive first half," Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson said after the draw. "We asked the lads for character and an improvement in the quality of our play second half and they did that brilliantly."

Hull, meanwhile, continued to tick along in fifth as they took a point at Oxford, despite leading at the Kassam Stadium. Six games to go and a play-off spot remains firmly in their grasp.

"We should be happy with a point, this is maybe a great result today," said Hull boss Sergij Jakirovic. "It's always the main target to take three points, but it was an opponent today who was good and we should be happy with 1-1.

"Our position in the league is good, we have everything in our own hands. We can blame nobody else, but ourselves from here."

Simeon Gholam

Clubs scrapping at the bottom show signs of resolve

Leicester 2-2 Preston | Norwich 1-1 Portsmouth | Oxford 1-1 Hull

Just a point separates 21st and 23rd in the table now, with Portsmouth just above the dotted line on 41 points, while Leicester and Oxford sit on 40 in the relegation zone.

All three picked up a draw on Good Friday, with Portsmouth nicking a 1-1 at Norwich as Pelle Mattsson scored at both ends for the Canaries.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Norwich City and Portsmouth.

It was a huge result for Pompey, especially considering the form Norwich are in and the way they fell apart at QPR to lose 6-1 before the international break.

“I am really pleased with both the point and the performance after what happened in our last match,” said boss John Mousinho. “It was just what we needed going into another big game on Monday [against Oxford]."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Oxford United and Hull City.

Oxford themselves hit back from behind to draw 1-1 against Hull City, they head to Fratton Park for the lunchtime kick-off on Easter Monday.

“Unfortunately for us it wasn’t to be, but in terms of effort, endeavour, creativity - the feeling in the crowd which was incredible," said U's boss Matt Bloomfield.

"It’s not easy against a team like Hull to come back from a goal down either so there’s lots to be pleased with. Now we have to focus on repeating that performance for the last six games."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship game between Leicester City and Preston North End.

Sandwiched between those two sides is Leicester, who led, trailed and then finally earned a 2-2 draw against Preston. Patson Daka scoring both goals for the Foxes at the King Power Stadium.

“It’s up to us," said Leicester boss Gary Rowett. "It’s making sure we stay united, but ultimately we’ve got to win games of football. If you don’t, then you don’t deserve to get above other teams.

“Since I’ve been here, we’ve been incredibly competitive. We’ve been on the better end of the performances. We should have more points than we have. So we’ve got to make sure we get those points.”

Simeon Gholam

Sports.title: The Glen Rovers claims Easter Classic prize
Sports.content:
The Glen Rovers sprang a 33-1 surprise in the Midnite All-Weather Easter Classic Middle Distance Handicap at Newcastle.

With £175,000 on offer a competitive field had assembled, including one from the all-conquering Willie Mullins yard in Gaucher, ridden by champion all-weather jockey Billy Loughnane.

He appeared to have everything covered going into the final furlong and hitting the front but Sean D Bowen, himself champion apprentice in 2024, was coolness personified before making his challenge, winning by half a length.

Trained by Lucy Wadham, better known for her handling of jumpers - and indeed The Glen Rovers started his life in a bumper - he provided his enthusiastic part-owner Conor Ryan, who works for Charlie Appleby, with one of the best days of his life.

Ryan said: "We've had him a couple of years now, he's been a bit difficult to train but Lucy and the team at home have done a fantastic job with him.

"The team in the yard have done a great job, it's been a big team effort and he's been put back together a couple of times but Lucy has looked after him.

"He just took his time to come to fruition this season, a couple of small issues he had, but had to run him to get him fit but he came into this race today way overpriced.

"We were pretty confident he'd run well, we knew the trip would suit and he'd won here before.

"This horse has changed my and my family's life, that is what being involved in a racehorse can do to you."

Bowen said: "He was very good, he's two from two here now. I was able to get cover from a wide draw and that made the difference.

"Lucy and the team, and Conor at home have done a great job, I can't thank them enough for the opportunity.

"He's top heavy so he takes a few runs to get into the swing of things.

"Just over three furlongs out I had to take him back off the horse in front of me, that was when I thought we had a chance and I was always getting there."

Tyrrhenian Sea gets revenge on Chancellor

Tyrrhenian Sea has been a fixture of the all-weather scene for five years now and showed at the age of eight the fire still burns bright when displaying a sparkling turn of foot in the BetMGM All-Weather Championships Mile Handicap at Newcastle.

Since making a winning debut at Gosforth Park in December 2021, a total of 17 of 24 career races have been on an artificial surface for Roger Varian's extraordinarily striking eight-year-old.

He has won twice at Listed level and was second to Chancellor in the Tandridge Stakes when attempting back-to-back wins in that contest last time out. This time, 3lb better off for a length with John and Thady Gosden's one-time Classic hope, he won by a length and a quarter from Blue Rc.

Jack Mitchell has ridden him more than any other jockey and said: "He's a horse who has always had a special place in my heart all through his career. As an eight-year-old against younger horses I thought he'd have to be at his very best today.

"I was travelling so well, but I was trying to find a way through being drawn 14, then I followed Rab (Havlin on Chancellor) and he picked up really well.

Image: Tyrrhenian Sea proved too good at Gosforth Park

"He stays further so Roger and the team had some deep discussions over whether to run in this or the Easter Classic, this looked the tougher race but we went a nice gallop and we were 3lb better with Chancellor.

"His best form is on the all-weather so as long as he's fit and healthy he'll come back and have another go next year."

Best of the rest

Andrew Balding's Stateira looked the banker on the card and she duly obliged as the 11-8 favourite in the BetMGM Fillies' And Mares' Championships Handicap.

Having impressed when winning at the trials meeting 72 days ago, Balding decided to bide his time and wait for the £150,000 final and it paid dividends.

Despite being 10lb higher, Oisin Murphy oozed confidence and she looks well worth a crack at a black-type race.

"She was entitled to be favourite, but I was just a bit concerned that we'd have to chance plans as she normally likes to get on with it at her own speed," said Murphy.

"I thought if I rode her that way today she'd do too much into the headwind, but I was pleased with how she settled, she went to sleep and she was entitled to win.

"The ones in front were slowing down before I asked her a question. She's in great health at the moment and when fillies are in that space they can really improve.

"Andrew will have a good think about what to do next, but today was a good target for her."

On some of his best form William Haggas' Wiltshire looked well handicapped in the Midnite All-Weather Sprint Handicap but he had developed a propensity to be slowly away.

However, he broke on terms this time and the 7-1 chance moved smoothly into contention under Cieren Fallon, who followed Fivethousandtoone through before scooting clear to win by a length.

Haggas' wife and assistant Maureen said: "He finally had to had a wind op and combined with the tongue tie he seemed happier. He's always had the ability, we know that.

"He enjoys the all-weather and when he's on the grass he doesn't want it too quick. He needed that, a nice confidence boost.

"Cieren knows him well and he's good at cool rides. He jumped much better today which helped.

"He had a trapped epiglottis and it made him sound like a distressed pug!"

Sports.title: Rudoni returns with a double as Coventry move closer to promotion
Sports.content:
Coventry City moved a step closer to the Premier League with a pulsating 3-2 win over Derby as Jack Rudoni scored twice on his return from injury.

The Rams proved a pesky opponent for Coventry to crack, twice pegging back the Championship leaders but Rudoni, who sprung from the bench on 62 minutes, scored the second of his two goals with 10 minutes remaining.

The midfielder had been out of action since February 28 but returned to devastating effect as Coventry made it eight wins in nine league outings.

The win means Coventry are 11 points clear at the top and need just eight points from their remaining six games to secure a Premier League return.

Frank Onyeka got Coventry off to the perfect start, curling home a fabulous effort from range but Ben Brereton Diaz headed home an equaliser courtesy of a sensational cross from Matt Clarke.

Lampard, who led Derby to the Championship play off final in 2019, made a triple sub just after the hour mark and four minutes later it paid dividends.

Both teams squandered chances before Rudoni showed how it's done when firing home from 15 yards.

Derby kept asking questions though and won a penalty when Brereton Diaz was adjudged to have been fouled by Carl Rushworth despite the goalkeeper getting a touch on the ball.

Brereton Diaz dispatched the penalty but just three minutes Rudoni struck again to leave the home fans signing about winning the league.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Rudoni's 'brilliant' finish puts Coventry ahead for the third time against Derby.

The managers

Coventry's Frank Lampard:

"Enjoy it while it's there because we don't always get these nights and these results and we've had a lot of them this season.

"Now they can enjoy it, they're a massive part of what we do here, the fans are incredible.

"Both teams took part in a great game of football and we've come out on top.

"It was a great night of football, I really enjoyed the game. Elements I didn't love, elements I really liked.

"But we come away with a win. This team has got character."

Derby's John Eustace:

"I thought we were excellent. It was really pleasing to come to the best team in the league and perform how we did.

"It showed good signs for us. We had two or three missing and we've certainly not let anyone down.

"We'd started well before they scored, then we showed great character to come back into it.

"I'm disappointed to lose. The three goals we conceded were all sloppy and we could have scored a couple more ourselves if we'd been more clinical.

"We've got six big games coming up now that we'll be ready for."
